## Are the items fair?

### Differential item functioning

An item shows **differential item functioning (DIF)** when people of the
same ability but from different groups (here, `r paste(levels(group), collapse = " and ")`)
have different chances of getting it right. A difference in the groups'
*average* scores is not DIF by itself; it may reflect a real difference in
ability (impact).

`dif()` tests each item in turn with a likelihood-ratio test, using the
other items as anchors. It can take up to a minute.

```{r {{id}}-dif, exercise = TRUE, exercise.timelimit = 300}
res <- dif(resp, group = group, model = models[2])
res
```

```{r {{id}}-dif-check}
lab_need(exists("res") && inherits(res, "mv_dif"), "Save the result of dif() as `res`.")
paste0(sum(res$table$flag), " item(s) are flagged after the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.")
```

```{r {{id}}-q-dif}
.tk_res <- mirtverse::dif(resp, group = group, model = models[2])
.tk_k <- sum(.tk_res$table$flag)
.tk_opts <- sort(utils::head(unique(pmax(0, .tk_k + c(0, -1, 1, 2, -2, 3, 4))), 4))
.tk_flag <- paste(.tk_res$table$item[.tk_res$table$flag], collapse = ", ")
do.call(question_radio, c(
  list("How many items does dif() flag?"),
  lapply(.tk_opts, function(k) answer(as.character(k), correct = k == .tk_k,
    message = if (k == .tk_k) {
      if (.tk_k == 0) "Right: no item is flagged." else paste0("Right: ", .tk_flag, ". A flag starts a content review; it does not prove bias.")
    } else "Count the flagged rows in the table that dif() prints.")),
  list(allow_retry = TRUE)))
```
